newsitem.title: UK: Rugby says second-half outlook mixed.
newsitem.headline: Rugby says second-half outlook mixed.

text.p: British Building materials company Rugby Group Plc said the outlook for the second half of this year was mixed after reporting a 19.7 percent drop in first-half pre-tax profits.
The first half was affected by adverse weather in the UK, U.S. and Continental Europe and a drop in construction activity.

Rugby said its European joinery operations and Pioneer were expected to continue to perform well and that market conditions in the United States had generally improved. However, this was not the case in either Australia or the U.K.

"In the U.K., there are some signs of modest improvement in the housing market, though these will be slow to flow through to our business and are largely offset by reductions in public infrastructure spend," Rugby said in a statement.

Rugby earlier reported pre-tax profits of 29.0 million pounds, topping analysts' forecasts which ranged from 26.5 million to 28.5 million. It said its cash position was strong with gearing below 10 percent.
The firm said that in the U.K. the sharp fall it saw in construction activity in the second half of 1995 carried through into 1996 and it saw little improvement in market conditions.
Rugby said cement sales were eight percent lower and competition in the joinery market did not abate with the result that profits in that unit were halved.
However, in Europe joinery operations traded well despite difficult conditions in Germany.
Also on the positive side, the metal products performance was satisfactory and in Australia Cockburn performed steadily, helped by higher land sales.
In the U.S., Rugby said profits at Pioneer Plastics were well ahead of the same time last year but it was difficult to improve margins at Rugby Building Products.
